title: Switch Character Roles
use_cases: Use when developing complex character backgrounds to avoid clichés
Implement when designing unique personality traits for secondary characters
Configure when drafting plot points that require unexpected character behavior
Use when reviewing a manuscript to ensure characters are three-dimensional
content: The villain lives happily ever after. Instead of a wise old man, a child is the sage or mentor. The love interest turns the protagonist down for good. Like with these examples, try mixing up some minor tropes. Every human being—or fae or werewolf or other species—is unique, and using stereotypes as the basis for descriptions or actions will turn away readers. Be creative when it comes to blending who your characters are with what they say and do. The tough bodyguard who doesn’t put up with any tomfoolery also knits with people in a retirement community.
